title: Eat thy bread with joy (Ecclesiastes 9:7–10)
hookLine: enjoy your life, and do what your hand finds to do with all your might

cards: Lunch, eaten standing up. One hand holds the sandwich, the other scrolls. Somewhere around the fourth bite the sandwich is gone, and there's no memory of how it tasted.
The mind was three meetings ahead the whole time. Now listen to who's about to talk about this: Kohelet, the man who said all is breath, who watched the wise die like the foolish.
You might expect him to say food doesn't matter either. He says the opposite.

teach.h: GO THY WAY, EAT THY BREAD.
teach.b: Ecclesiastes nine, in the King James words: "Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works." Go thy way: almost a dismissal. Stop worrying, go and eat.
And the reason isn't that you've earned it.
God now accepteth thy works. In his telling, the meal isn't a reward to be won later; the acceptance has come first. Then Kohelet piles up ordinary gifts.

Let your clothes be white, and your head not lack oil: dress for a good day. Live joyfully with the wife you love, all the days of your fleeting life. The Hebrew for those days is the word from a few days ago, hevel.

teach.h: ENJOY IT BECAUSE IT IS BREATH.
teach.b: Kohelet doesn't say enjoy life because it lasts. He says enjoy it because it doesn't. Breath is short, so taste the bread.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER THY HAND FINDETH TO DO.
teach.b: Then the verse that gives the joy some muscle: "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest."
A sobering reason, given straight. The work in front of you is yours now, not later. So this isn't a call to idle pleasure.
It's two halves of one way of living: eat with joy, and work with your whole strength. Some readers hear these lines as the quiet heart of the whole book, where its doubt and its gladness meet.

how: Before eating bread, Jews say a blessing, hamotzi, thanking God who brings forth bread from the earth, and after the meal they say a grace, Birkat Hamazon.

games.q: you're Kohelet. you've said all is breath, and that the wise die like fools. what do you tell people to do?
o: eat with joy and work with all your might.
games.why: go thy way, eat thy bread with joy: because life is breath, he tells us to taste it and to work while we can.

practice: Picture the next thing you'll eat, its color, its smell, the first bite, eaten sitting down with the phone out of reach, slowly enough to taste it, and then the moment after, when you stand and turn to whatever your hand finds to do.
Jewish practice sets a blessing before eating; if you pray, you can say the one you know, and if not, a moment of thanks is enough.
